description.en: To encourage good behavior and work among inmates in the prison, they are granted special remission in their sentence.

desc.en: Remission earned monthly for factory work and good behavior.
Remission granted by the government on national festivals or special occasions.

description.en: The mushroom project is an innovative initiative, producing nutritious mushrooms in small spaces and short times.

desc.en: Production of protein-rich mushrooms.
Farming with modern methods in small spaces.
High demand for mushrooms in the market.

description.en: Mushrooms are cultivated in climate-controlled rooms. High-quality mushrooms are produced by properly regulating temperature, humidity, and light. It is a glimpse of modern farming that goes beyond the limits of traditional agriculture.

Mushroom cultivation is a highly skilled job. Inmates are taught sterilization and cultivation techniques. This innovative training builds their confidence and connects them with modern agricultural technology.
A gymnasium with modern equipment has been made available in the prison for the physical fitness and mental well-being of the inmates.

desc.en: Various exercise machines and weights available.
Organizing sports competitions to build team spirit among inmates.

description.en: A smart card-based phone facility is available to allow inmates to maintain regular contact with their families. This includes both audio and video calling options.

desc.en: Facility to communicate on registered mobile or landline using a smart card.
Opportunity to speak face-to-face with family through special video calling booths.

description.en: A new direction in rehabilitation through discipline, skills, labor, and self-reliance.
Building skills and responsibility through farming and allied activities.
Empowerment through vocational training and productive activities.

title.en: Opportunity for Labor, Direction for Future.

description.en: Fostering skill, discipline, and self-belief through productive work.
Getting ready for reintegration into society through responsibility and self-sufficiency.

quote.en: Security, correction, and rehabilitation are our guiding pillars. We are committed to equipping inmates with skills to make them productive members of society.

desc.en: The main high-security prison was built by the British. It later became historically significant for housing prominent freedom fighters like Mahatma Gandhi and Lokmanya Tilak.
The historic Poona Pact was signed within the Yerawada complex under a mango tree between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
The Yerawada Open Jail was established on the prison's agricultural lands, introducing a trust-based rehabilitative model without high boundary walls.
The Government of Maharashtra launched a jail tourism initiative, allowing students and historians to visit the historic yards within the campus.

description.en: Established to facilitate the gradual reintegration of long-term convicts into society, the Open Jail operates without high walls or strict confinements. Inmates who demonstrate impeccable conduct during their initial sentences in closed prisons are transferred here.

subtitle.en: Path of Transformation through Labor and Trust

description.en: Spread across a sprawling campus in Pune, the Yerawada Open Jail represents a paradigm shift from punitive incarceration to rehabilitative correction. Operating on minimum security and high trust, it prepares inmates for a productive and self-reliant life after release.

desc.en: Inmates of Yerawada Open Prison engaged in farming activities, learning modern agricultural methods, organic crop production, and harvesting on farmlands.
A greenhouse nursery program where inmates are trained in scientific horticulture, composting, and cultivating quality plants for a greener environment.
Inmates learning dairy farming, cattle care, milk production, and livestock management, supporting self-sustainability.
Training in poultry farming, including feeding, care, disease control, and poultry farm management for inmates.
K. K. Mangal Lawn is a spacious wedding and event venue managed and maintained by Yerawada Open Prison inmates, providing landscaping and gardening training.
An industrial power loom factory where inmates produce fabrics for government use, developing advanced textile manufacturing and operations skills.
An industrial collaboration with Minda Industries, where inmates are trained in automotive wire harnessing assembly, promoting advanced industrial skills.
Inmates undergoing vocational training in bricklaying, cement mixing, and masonry construction to build vocational skills.
A professional ironing and laundry service department operated by inmates at Yerawada, training them in commercial laundry operations and garment care.
A commercial-grade laundry facility at Yerawada Central Jail, providing garment washing and ironing services with focus on hygiene and dignity.
A vocational salon unit operated by inmates providing professional training in haircutting, grooming, and personal care services for self-reliance.
A popular open-air canteen serving delicious, home-style meals prepared under strict hygiene standards by Yerawada Open Jail inmates.
A fully equipped indoor gym facility inside the prison premises to encourage physical fitness, strength training, and active health among inmates.

description.en: Established to facilitate the gradual reintegration of long-term convicts into society, the Open Jail operates without high walls or strict confinements. Inmates who demonstrate impeccable conduct during their initial sentences in closed prisons are transferred here.
A nursery of various fruit and flower plants has been developed in the prison, providing skill training to inmates.

desc.en: Production of fruit, flower, and ornamental plants.
Scientific training to inmates on plant production and care.
Generating income for the prison by selling plants.

description.en: Through the nursery, we do not just produce saplings but make a significant contribution to maintaining the balance of nature. Various medicinal and ornamental plants are nurtured here with utmost care. This initiative not only turns the prison premises green but also spreads the message of environmental conservation.

Working with plants has a profoundly positive impact on the mental health of inmates. Connecting with soil fosters patience, responsibility, and focus. It equips them with valuable vocational knowledge to potentially start their own business in the future.
Through dairy farming, milk and dairy products are produced in the prison, which is beneficial for health and income.

desc.en: Fresh milk available for sale inside and outside the prison.
Proper care of animals and fodder management.
Production of items like curd, buttermilk, and ghee.

description.en: Cows and buffaloes are taken care of exceptionally well in our sheds. Regular veterinary checkups, clean water, and nutritious fodder ensure the good health of the animals and yield high-quality milk.

The fresh milk produced adds nutritional value to the inmates' diet. Selling surplus milk and dairy products generates good financial profit for the prison. Working in the proximity of animals also instills peace and empathy in the inmates.
High-quality vermicompost is prepared from wet waste in the prison, promoting organic farming.

desc.en: Improving soil quality using natural fertilizers.
Disposal of wet waste in an eco-friendly manner.
Financial benefit by selling vermicompost.

description.en: Vermicompost is prepared by processing wet waste from the prison kitchen and farm foliage. This compost is highly beneficial for crops and increases soil fertility. It reduces dependence on chemical fertilizers.

This project has made 100% waste management within the prison possible. Awareness about the environment and organic farming has been created among the inmates. This initiative is a solid step towards 'Swachh Bharat' and sustainable development.
Combining modern techniques with traditional farming, many innovative agricultural activities and products are implemented in the prison.

desc.en: Use of new technology in agriculture.
Fruit processing and value-added products.
Innovative efforts for the holistic progress of inmates.

description.en: Moving beyond traditional farming, agricultural experiments are being conducted using modern technologies like hydroponics, drip irrigation, and greenhouses. Along with this, agricultural produce is processed to create value-added products (e.g., pickles, jams).

Innovative activities give scope to the creativity of the inmates. They get lessons in product packaging, branding, and marketing, which develops entrepreneurship in them and gives them new confidence for their future life.
Goat farming aims to earn more profit with low investment. It is excellent vocational training for inmates.

desc.en: Financial stability by farming goats with small capital.
Production of high-quality meat.
Teaching inmates modern techniques of goat farming.

description.en: Goat farming is a rapidly growing business. Here, scientific management of vaccination, nutritious feed, and shelter for goats is ensured. The focus is on rearing high-quality breeds and improving their reproductive capacity and growth.

This project gives inmates practical knowledge of animal husbandry. This business, which can be done in a small space and with low capital, provides a sustainable way for inmates to reintegrate into society and live with dignity after their release.
Poultry farming involves egg and meat production. It provides employment to inmates and financial income to the prison.

desc.en: Direct employment for many inmates through poultry farming.
Scientific production of eggs and meat.
Sale of produced goods in the local market.

description.en: Modern and scientific methods are adopted in our poultry farm. Special emphasis is placed on the health of the birds, the quality of their feed, and their shelter, enabling the production of high-quality eggs and meat.

Inmates working in this sector gain knowledge of all technical aspects of poultry farming. It builds their confidence to start their own business and stand on their own feet post-release. Furthermore, it aids in increasing the financial self-sufficiency of the prison.
To maintain inmates' ties with their families and prepare them for reintegration into society, Furlough and Parole leaves are granted as per regulations.

desc.en: Leave granted to eligible inmates every year for a certain number of days to visit their family.
Leave granted for special reasons like serious family illness, marriage, or death.

subtitle.en: Special Room for Female Inmates and Children

description.en: A safe and comfortable 'Hirkani Room' has been created in the prison for breastfeeding and playing for the young children living with female inmates.

desc.en: A private space for mothers to breastfeed their children in a safe environment.
Toys, pictures, and entertainment tools for young children.

description.en: A wet canteen is operated to allow inmates to purchase tea, coffee, and fresh snacks using their personal money (PPC).

desc.en: Hot tea, Poha, Upma etc. available every morning and evening.
All transactions in the canteen are done via smart cards or token systems.

description.en: Facilities are available to make illiterate inmates literate and to provide degree/post-graduate education (e.g. through YCMOU or IGNOU) to those willing to learn.

desc.en: Teaching illiterate inmates how to read and write.
Opportunity to pursue degree courses through YCMOU and IGNOU.

description.en: A commercial-grade laundry and ironing facility at Yerawada Prison, providing professional garment washing and pressing services. This equips inmates with the technical knowledge to run commercial laundries.

desc.en: Clean washing using high-capacity commercial machines.
Training in modern steam ironing technology.
Garment sanitization for health and hygiene.

description.en: Managed and maintained by Yerawada Open Prison inmates, this is a spacious wedding and event venue. This initiative provides inmates with training in landscaping, gardening, and event management. The walls of the lawn feature beautiful traditional murals painted by the inmates themselves.
